definition.en: The World Health Organization (WHO) is a specialized agency of the United Nations responsible for international public health, setting global standards, and coordinating responses to health emergencies.
definition.hi: The World Health Organization (WHO) is a specialized agency of the United Nations responsible for international public health, setting global standards, and coordinating responses to health emergencies.

importanceInUpsc.en: For UPSC GS-3, understanding the WHO is crucial as it intersects with social infrastructure, human capital development, and global economic governance. It provides the framework for international health cooperation which directly impacts India's public health expenditure and policy formulation.

learningOutcomes.en: Understand the organizational structure and mandate of the WHO.

learningOutcomes.en: Analyze the role of WHO in shaping global health policies and their implications for the Indian economy.
